events.title: DeepSeek V3 released
events.summary: DeepSeek released V3 on December 26, 2024 — a 671B-parameter MoE model with open weights, strong coding results, and training costs far below Western frontier labs.
events.about: DeepSeek V3 preceded R1 and proved Chinese labs could ship competitive open-weight MoE models at scale. Its MIT-licensed weights and transparent training details made it a default choice for self-hosted inference — and a wake-up call on AI compute economics before the R1 reasoning shock in January.

narrative.whyChosen: DeepSeek V3 showed open MoE models could rival closed APIs before the R1 reasoning wave.
narrative.whyImportant: It shifted assumptions about who could afford frontier-scale training and release open weights.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams wanted strong coding and general models without proprietary API lock-in or Western-only vendors.

events.title: Google Gemini 2.0 Flash released
events.summary: Google released Gemini 2.0 Flash on December 11, 2024 — a multimodal agentic model with native image and audio output, tool use, and twice the speed of 1.5 Pro.
events.about: Gemini 2.0 Flash launched Google's agentic era: multimodal live APIs, Deep Research in Gemini Advanced, and native tool calling for Search and code execution. It outperformed 1.5 Pro on key benchmarks at Flash-tier latency — keeping Google competitive in the year-end race with OpenAI's o1 and Sora releases.

narrative.whyChosen: Gemini 2.0 reframed Google's models around agents, multimodal output, and low latency.
narrative.whyImportant: Native multimodal generation and tool use became baseline expectations for frontier models.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers needed faster Gemini models that could act, not just answer, across modalities.

events.title: OpenAI o3 reasoning models announced
events.summary: OpenAI announced o3 and o3-mini on December 20, 2024 — successors to o1 with stronger math, coding, and science reasoning, offered first to safety researchers.
events.about: The o3 reveal closed OpenAI's '12 Days of OpenAI' with a direct answer to Google's Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking. Sam Altman said o3-mini would ship by late January and full o3 shortly after — escalating the inference-time reasoning arms race that DeepSeek R1 would later join with open weights.

narrative.whyChosen: o3 signaled the next generation of OpenAI reasoning models before public release.
narrative.whyImportant: It kept frontier labs competing on test-time compute, not just parameter count.
narrative.problemSolved: o1-class reasoning needed a successor for harder STEM, coding, and agent benchmarks.
